html:
The fifth king of the Chakri dynasty of Siam, known as Rama V, who reigned from 1868 to 1910. He modernised the kingdom and kept it independent while Britain and France took everything around it.

He was the son of Mongkut, who had opened Siam to the West with the Bowring Treaty. Chulalongkorn came to the throne at 15. His main reforms:

  • He ended slavery in stages, from a decree in 1874 to the abolition act of 1905.
  • He replaced the old court offices with ministries on a European model and brought distant provinces under central control.
  • He built railways, telegraphs, schools and a modern army, and sent his sons to study in Europe.
  • He travelled to Europe twice, meeting its monarchs as an equal.

The price of independence was land. After the Franco-Siamese crisis of 1893 he gave up Laos to French Indochina, and in 1909 he ceded four Malay states to Britain. Siam stayed the only country in Southeast Asia never colonised. Thais honour him as "the Beloved Great King".
